messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: p99 latency for /v1/generate exceeded SLO (p99=7.2s, SLO=1.5s) in us-west-2. Auto-alert triggered. Paging oncall. Dash: https://dash.redwood/local/latency?range=5m

pagerduty: Paging leo (oncall) and maya (sre). :pager:

leo: Acked. I'm on it, will join incident channel.

maya: Ack. grabbing dashboards now. I can see p95 and p99 spiking starting ~03:10 UTC.

jin: Noted. any recent deploys or config changes? I see a canary rollout to model-neo-qa-2 ~03:07.

alex: Also saw a batching policy tweak rolled out ~03:00 (reduced max_batch_time from 8ms -> 2ms) by @deploy-bot.

leo: Good leads. @jin can you pull runtime logs for any stream_stall errors and kv cache hit rates? I'll check routing and autoscaler.

jin: Pulling logs... tail from runtime nodes in us-west-2:
```text
[03:12:30] gpu-08 queue_depth=48 max_batch=64 batch_wait_ms=15 kv_cache_hit=0.12
[03:12:31] gpu-09 queue_depth=52 max_batch=64 batch_wait_ms=17 kv_cache_hit=0.09
[03:12:32] serve.error: stream_stall: stall_count=22 tail_latency_ms=7200
```

maya: kv_cache_hit is very low, looks like a cold cache after the canary swap. Also batch_wait_ms jumped — batching/backpressure seems to be adding tail latency.

leo: Quick checklist: 1) is autoscaler able to add capacity? 2) any node OOMs or kernel alerts? 3) network errors/latency?

ops-bot: Autoscaler event: scale_up requested at 03:11:55, success=false, reason="allocation timeout". Recent allocation failures in us-west-2.

alex: Allocation timeouts align with spot contention in us-west-2 earlier this hour. Suggest routing fallback to a smaller model/pool in another AZ while we stabilize.

leo: Mitigation proposal (immediate):
- enable routing fallback to model-neo-qa-1 (smaller, warm cache)
- rollback batching policy change
- attempt alternative instance family for autoscaler
- notify customers & update status page

maya: I'm rolling the routing fallback and will revert batching config. Starting canary rollback now.

jin: Applying routing fallback: `PATCH /routing/policies/active -d '{"fallback":"model-neo-qa-1","threshold_p99":1.5}'` -> accepted.

ops-bot: Routing policy change deployed across control plane (6s).

leo: Rolling back batching policy to previous values.

deploy-bot: Rolling back config: `configs/batching/last` -> success.

incident-bot: Update: p99 dropped to 2.1s after mitigation (p95=0.9s) — improving but still above SLO. Dash: https://dash.redwood/local/latency?range=10m

maya: Autoscaler now able to place instances using alt instance family in us-west-2b. ops-bot shows +6 nodes added and healthy.

ops-bot: New instances are healthy and joined serving pool.

jin: Runtime snapshot after mitigations:
```text
[03:19:10] gpu-08 queue_depth=22 batch_wait_ms=6 kv_cache_hit=0.45
[03:19:11] gpu-09 queue_depth=18 batch_wait_ms=5 kv_cache_hit=0.48
```

leo: Nice. Customer impact estimate: ~0.8% of total requests affected over the 12m window, streaming endpoints worse (~1.7%) due to stalls and client retries.

alex: Drafting customer-facing note and updating status page. ETA for full recovery 20-30m if no regressions.

maya: Handoff plan: I'll continue active watch for 30m, then hand to @jin for follow-up. Summary for handoff: likely root cause = batching policy change + canary model leading to cold KV cache + autoscaler allocation timeouts under spot pressure.

jin: I'll monitor tail latencies and run a deeper mem/kernel check: `sudo journalctl -u runtime -n 200 | grep stall`.

leo: Thanks team. I'll keep channel open for 30m and reopen paging if we see regression. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident status update: Severity=P1 -> mitigation in-place, recovery in progress. This channel will be archived after stabilization and a follow-up postmortem will be created.
